A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and are complete and readable. The main text, nine figures, Algorithm 1, equations, and Appendices A.1–A.3 support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 experiments measuring path curvature, projected optimization dynamics, and linear mode connectivity, including supplementary results in Appendix A.3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their results in Figures 2–9, including the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The model architectures, AutoNEB path construction, Hessian/Fisher curvature estimates, and k-step projected SGD procedure in Algorithm 1 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 image classification and examine the same nonlinear-path and linear mode-connectivity scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 4 retains the same comparison of vanilla SGD, Adam, and SGD with Nesterov momentum. No evaluated comparator is added, removed, or revised elsewhere.

E3.justification: The default 200-epoch training with batch size 256, augmentation, AutoNEB refinement cycles, curvature measurements, splitting-epoch experiments, and k=15 projection setting remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The starting-position, batch-size, learning-rate, and optimizer analyses are retained. Appendix analyses of path geometry and relaxation-time scaling also remain unchanged (Figures 7–8).

E5.justification: Descriptions of AutoNEB random seeds and repeated SGD realizations, along with existing error bars and shaded bands, are unchanged. No run counts or uncertainty procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Figures 2–9 retain identical plotted results and captions. Findings about interior-path curvature, relaxation toward endpoints, and the longer persistence of curvature barriers are unchanged; no result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The entropic-force derivation in Section 2 and Hessian/Fisher reasoning in Appendix A.2 are unchanged. Equations 7–8 move from page 13 to page 14 without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1.2 contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about curvature-induced confinement and entropic barriers persisting longer than energetic barriers.

C2.justification: Section 5 retains the same interpretations concerning late-training localization, generalization, and weight averaging, plus the limitation concerning biased path selection. The new ethics statement adds no substantive scientific qualification.

D1.justification: v2 adds a Reproducibility Statement promising codebase release when the author list is unblinded. This is new release information, but it provides no code link, additional implementation settings, or evidence that release has occurred.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and cited works are unchanged. References shift across pages without additions, removals, or changes to research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds brief Ethics and Reproducibility Statements before the references, including disclosure of language-model-assisted text polishing, and an ICLR 2026 publication header. Existing scientific prose and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The conference header and horizontal rule are added, and the new statements shift reference and appendix layout. Figure 7 moves lower on page 14; all figures and Algorithm 1 retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The scientific evidence, methods, theory, claims, and limitations are unchanged. The ethics disclosure and conditional code-release promise add limited transparency but no technical detail or code link. Together with the publication header and layout shifts, these additions do not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
